{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-05",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Deletion request intake", "Support console", "Main database", "Analytics warehouse", "Application logs", "Backup system"],
    "dataStores": ["Main database", "Analytics warehouse", "Application logs", "Backups"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Customer to support", "Support console to main database", "Main database to warehouse/backup replication"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Deleted customers' personal data stays readable in the warehouse, logs and backups",
      "scenario": "A customer exercises their deletion right. Only the main database row is flagged deleted, so a warehouse analyst, a log reader or anyone who obtains a backup can still read that person's full personal data indefinitely. Any later breach of those stores exposes people who believe they were deleted, and the design has no propagation or retention cut-off for the copies.",
      "component": "Analytics warehouse, application logs, backups",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Copies in the warehouse, logs and backups are left as is." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-212", "CWE-359"],
      "plainLanguage": "When someone asks to be deleted, their data is still sitting in the data warehouse, logs and backups.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Propagate deletion to every copy of the customer's data",
        "given": "an accepted account deletion request",
        "when": "the deletion is executed",
        "then": "personal data is erased or irreversibly anonymised in the warehouse and logs within a defined window, and backups carry a documented expiry after which the data is unrecoverable, with the outcome recorded per store"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Soft-delete flag leaves the live record present and reachable by code paths that ignore the flag",
      "scenario": "Deletion is only a status change in the main database, so the record and its personal fields still exist. Any report, API endpoint, job or support screen that does not filter on the deleted flag keeps returning the person's data, and the account can be silently reactivated. An attacker who finds one unfiltered endpoint reads data about people who were told they were deleted.",
      "component": "Main database / application read paths",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Support marks the account as deleted in the main database." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-212"],
      "plainLanguage": "The account is only flagged as deleted, so any screen or report that forgets to check the flag still shows the person's data.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Hard-delete or tokenise personal fields on the primary record",
        "given": "an account marked for deletion",
        "when": "the deletion job runs",
        "then": "personal fields on the primary record are removed or replaced with non-identifying tokens so no read path can return them, and remaining references keep only a non-personal identifier"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Deletion requests are actioned without proving the requester owns the account",
      "scenario": "The design says customers can request deletion and support then marks the account deleted, with no identity verification step described. An attacker who knows a victim's email or account details contacts support and has the victim's account destroyed, or conversely requests deletion of a competitor's business account, causing loss of access and data.",
      "component": "Deletion request intake / support console",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers can request account deletion. Support marks the account as deleted in the main database." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-640", "CWE-862"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could ask support to delete another person's account by pretending to be them.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Verify the requester before executing a deletion",
        "given": "an incoming deletion request",
        "when": "support prepares to action it",
        "then": "the request is only executed after the account owner is authenticated through a channel bound to the account (for example a signed-in confirmation or a one-time link to the registered address), and unverified requests are rejected"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Any support agent can destroy any account with no authorisation limits or second pair of eyes",
      "scenario": "Deletion is performed by support directly against the main database with no described restriction on which agents may do it or which accounts they may touch. A compromised or malicious support account can mass-delete customers, including high-value or enterprise accounts, in a single session.",
      "component": "Support console to main database",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Support marks the account as deleted in the main database." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-285", "CWE-269"],
      "plainLanguage": "One support login can wipe out any customer account, with nothing stopping a stolen or misused account.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict and throttle the deletion capability",
        "given": "a support agent using the deletion function",
        "when": "they submit a deletion for an account",
        "then": "the action is allowed only for agents holding an explicit deletion permission, is bound to the specific verified request, and bulk or repeated deletions beyond a defined threshold require approval by a second authorised user"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No evidence of who asked for a deletion, who executed it, or which copies were erased",
      "scenario": "The design records only the deleted status on the account. When a customer disputes that they asked to be deleted, or a regulator asks for proof the erasure completed, nobody can show who requested it, which agent performed it, when, or what happened to the warehouse, log and backup copies. A malicious agent can delete an account and deny doing so.",
      "component": "Deletion workflow record-keeping",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers can request account deletion. Support marks the account as deleted in the main database." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "There is no trail showing who requested a deletion, who carried it out, or whether the copies were really removed.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Keep a tamper-resistant deletion case record",
        "given": "a deletion request is received",
        "when": "it is verified, executed and completed across stores",
        "then": "a non-personal case record captures the request source, the verification method, the acting agent, timestamps and the per-store erasure outcome, and support users cannot edit or remove it"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Restoring a backup or re-running a warehouse load resurrects deleted accounts",
      "scenario": "Because backups and warehouse copies are untouched, a routine restore or a reverse sync from the warehouse re-creates the record of a customer who was deleted, silently undoing the erasure and reintroducing their personal data into the live system. Nobody is alerted, so marketing or billing can start contacting a deleted person again.",
      "component": "Backup restore / warehouse pipeline",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Copies in the warehouse, logs and backups are left as is." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-212"],
      "plainLanguage": "If a backup is restored, deleted customers come back to life along with their data.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Re-apply deletions after any restore or reload",
        "given": "a backup restore or a warehouse reload that predates a completed deletion",
        "when": "the data is brought back into a system",
        "then": "a suppression list of completed deletions is replayed against the restored data before it is used, and any resurrected record is re-erased and reported"
      }
    }
  ]
}

        "then": "the request is only executed after the account owner is authenticated (in-session request or a signed confirmation link sent to the registered contact), and the verification result is recorded with the request"

    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",

      "scenario": "Deletion is a one-click flag set by support. A malicious or phished support account can mark arbitrary accounts, including high-value or administrator accounts, as deleted in bulk.       "component": "Support console / main application database",

      "stride": "Tampering",

        "when": "the deletion grace period ends",

    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",

      "scenario": "The design relies on every reader honouring a deleted marker. Any endpoint, report, export or email job that forgets the filter will keep returning the deleted customer's personal data, and existing sessions or API tokens for that account may still work, so the account is reachable after deletion. An attacker who already holds a stolen session for a deleted account keeps their access.",
